Railway Hose Coupling Heads: Specify the Complete Pneumatic Interface

Define coupling heads, seals, end fittings and length datums together so an inter-vehicle pneumatic hose quotation describes the correct assembly.

2026-11-14 · Braking · Ma'anshan Railwheel Industrial Technology Co., Ltd.

The visible head is only part of the connection

A coupling head, its sealing element, the flexible hose and the opposite end fitting form an assembly with several interfaces. Naming the head style does not define its complete specification. Start with the approved circuit and part number, and identify whether the required item is hose only, a fitted hose or a pneumatic half coupling. Preserve that distinction in the purchase description and document schedule.

Control the mating face and seal identity

A connection may appear mechanically similar while using a different seal or contact arrangement. Provide the mating-interface drawing and required seal identification. Where threaded connections occur at the other end, specify thread form, size, sealing method and relevant orientation. A thread designation alone does not define a sealing face. Photographs support identification but do not authorize substitution.

Engineering principle: an assembly dimension is a datum chain

A hose assembly length may include flexible material, inserted fitting lengths, collars and end-interface locations. Different reference planes can therefore produce different reported lengths for the same physical assembly. State the controlled datum chain directly on the assembly drawing and identify any condition in which the dimension is measured. Where orientation matters, identify its angular reference as well. This prevents a supplier from compensating for an undefined end dimension by changing hose cut length. It also makes bid comparisons auditable: the same dimension is being offered, not merely the same numerical label.

Define length from meaningful reference points

Overall length can be measured between different features. A quote should state the reference faces and measurement condition used in the approved assembly drawing. Clarify whether fitting orientation is controlled relative to the head. A supplier cutting the flexible portion to an informal tape measurement may deliver an assembly with the wrong installed geometry even when the reported number matches the inquiry.

Use the standard within its documented scope

The public DIN catalog identifies EN 15807 as a pneumatic half-coupling standard for railway applications. That title is not permission to apply it indiscriminately to every hose in a vehicle. Obtain the contractually applicable standard and identify its relationship to the approved assembly specification. Do not reproduce test pressures or acceptance values from an unrelated hose family.

Review evidence and shipping condition together

Specify required assembly identification, inspection results, functional testing and records using the approved acceptance basis. Ask whether seals and protective caps are included and how mating surfaces are protected in transport. Receiving staff should verify identity and completeness before the item enters stock. Installation, leak testing in the vehicle and service release must follow authorized maintenance instructions.

Application scenario

Illustrative scenario: two vendors quote the same hose length, but one measures from a fitting shoulder and the other from the coupling face. The buyer marks the actual reference planes on the assembly drawing and requires revised offers. This closes a geometry discrepancy before either vendor manufactures the hose.

Frequently asked questions

Is a palm-type head enough information for an order?

No. The head identity, mating interface, seal, hose, opposite fitting and complete assembly requirements must be established.

Can the reference illustration be used as a production drawing?

No. It shows a representative configuration, not controlled dimensions or an approved vehicle part.
